[shiprekt] Took one of these on our 5 week trip to Europe, was brilliant - hotels, airport, train between Prague-Budapest, airbnb etc.
[AyTrain] Dumb question but how does this travel router work? Do you pay for a single internet plan and share it with the family while on holidays?
[Gunther] It works via whatever internet you give it…just gotta be creative sometimes
Wifi Hotel / Airbnb / Airport – joins the public network, then gives you your own secure network that all your devices connect to.
Ethernet - plug into a hotel’s LAN port, often behind TVs, or Airbnb wireless routers if accessible.
Mobile data - Use a USB SIM 4G/5G modem or phone via WiFi/USB tether
[johnmelb] joins the public network, then gives you your own secure network that all your devices connect to.
It's a brilliant device and I love it (have this one, the previous GL-MT1300 model and a much older GL-AR150 model)
Just a note though:
If the public network you join is insecure, then just connecting through this device will not make it secure, unless you use it to set up VPN.
Your clients <->(secure) this router <-> (potentially insecure if no encryption) public network
Connecting through WPA2 to this device by itself does not suddenly make your entire connection secure.
[quick-dry] @johnmelb: though TBF, unless you were VPN-ing back to your own home network (or some other known secure LAN) and only accessing things on that network. But accessing the internet, you're passing beyond the firewall - whether it's whatever it is past your gateway, or past your VPN provider's gateway, it's all the wild and unknown full of ne'er do wells. (I think they just mean that other devices on the public network can't see your devices, they just run against your travel router)
Just as an add-on to johnmelb's praise for this unit, I have one too and it's excellent.
If you update this router to the current firmware, it can be setup to auto connect to multiple VPNs and run traffic out through them.
For mine I have it setup so any traffic addressed to my local home LANs subnet goes over ther wireguard back to home (a Flint 2 does wireguard server duty), and traffic to various other addresses/domains gets routed out through a few other VPNs to work around geoblocks.
[Broden] Whats the best way to do this if you also want a portable mobile data as well? Without hotspoting phone of course
[FLICKIT] When I'm travelling in my campervan for 6 month stints, I plug my Tel$tra wifi modem/router into the travel router (I assume the same could be done with the cheapie USB 4g modem sticks and the likes), then I connect my phone, tablet, lappy to the travel router… I often park near the free Telstra pink wifi phone boxes and other wifi sources at caravan parks or outside hotels, connect the travel router to them, and use them if I'm uploading bulk amounts to Youtube or such…
[quick-dry] the best way is to use an old phone (i.e. not your actual 'main' phone) and tether it to the hotspot wiht USB cable - especialy if you have an old phone that can support eSIM. THat'll give you access to the widest ranger of providers - physical, esim, and if they have an annoying app you have to use for bonus data or renewal.
I upgraded from the Opal to this (Beryl AX), it lives in my travel bag, and sees heavy use. The USB port for tethering supplies enough juice to charge an iPhone.
There are portable units that you can throw a SIM card in, but they're often network locked, or limited on frequencies, expensive, or all of the above. For domestic AU use, you can probably find them for cheap on marlketplace, for overseas use - I'd go the phone route.
[FLICKIT] Agree, I forgot about that, I haven't been on the road this year… I carry a cheap 'Motorola G54 5G' as a spare phone when travelling (I also use it for GPS/mapping on the motorbike so my main phone isn't in danger)…
I've purchased cheap/free big data Amaysim esims numerous times, I install them on the G54 and tethered it to the travel router to then use the data for my lappy… (like this free 90gb esim deal in 2024, I went through 6 of them uploading vids to Youtube, lol: https://www.ozbargain.com.au/node/854734 )
[rk1314] My provider has a lot of "planned maintenance" downtime and this has been a lifesaver.
